fns.desc: get_max_nss_capability() reads hecaps->optional[0..3] (bw==CHAN_WIDTH_160) or optional[4..7] (bw==CHAN_WIDTH_80P80) from an attacker-supplied HE Capabilities element without ever checking elems->he_capabilities_len. The element is only validated at parse time (line 381) against HE_CAPABILITIES_ELEM_MIN_LEN==21, which covers only the mandatory mac/phy-capab-info + basic (<=80MHz) MCS map fields - the 'optional' 160MHz/80+80MHz MCS-map octets (0, 4, or 8 extra bytes) are NOT guaranteed present. wpas_parse_connection_info()/events.c:3553-3560 (and the per-link variant at events.c:3487-3497) call get_max_nss_capability(&resp_elems, ..., bw) where bw can be driven to CHAN_WIDTH_160/80P80 via get_sta_operation_chan_width(ap_cw, sta_cw) using the AP's own advertised (attacker-controlled) HE/VHT Operation channel width, independent of whether the AP's actual HE Capabilities IE in the same response included the extra optional octets. A malicious AP sending a minimal (21-byte) HE Capabilities IE alongside a wide-bandwidth HE/VHT Operation IE causes a 4-8 byte out-of-bounds read past the parsed IE buffer in wpa_supplicant when processing its own association response - closest CERT-C rule is ARR30-C (forming/using an out-of-bounds array subscript); could also be framed as API00-C (missing length validation before use).
